name: Linux Networking
tagline: Namespaces, veth, bridges, routing, NAT, VRRP, SSH and DNS: the on-prem plumbing.

howItWorks.title: Namespaces
howItWorks.body:
A namespace is an isolated network stack.
It owns its interfaces, routes, ARP table and firewall.
A container is a process inside one.

howItWorks.title: veth pairs and bridges
howItWorks.body:
A veth pair is a virtual cable: frames entering one end exit the other.
Attach one end to a bridge and it switches by MAC.
bridge fdb show lists the learned addresses.

howItWorks.title: Routing and forwarding
howItWorks.body:
The kernel picks the longest prefix match, then ARPs for the next hop.
A host routes between subnets only when net.ipv4.ip_forward=1.
Return traffic needs a route back.

howItWorks.title: NAT and netfilter
howItWorks.body:
MASQUERADE in nat POSTROUTING rewrites private sources to the uplink address.
conntrack remembers each flow and un-NATs replies.
The FORWARD chain decides what may cross.

howItWorks.title: VRRP, SSH and DNS
howItWorks.body:
VRRP gives the higher-priority node the VIP; a track_script drives failover.
sshd takes keys only, no root, named users.
dnsmasq serves A and PTR records and forwards the rest.

howItWorks.title: What sits in front
howItWorks.body:
Users and clients arrive at the Edge, usually a load balancer holding a virtual IP.
keepalived VRRP floats that VIP between two nodes for failover.
Switches and routers on the physical network deliver frames to the NIC (Infrastructure).
DNS records, for example from dnsmasq, point names at those addresses.

howItWorks.title: What sits behind
howItWorks.body:
Namespaces, veth pairs and bridges connect containers and VMs to the host.
The Docker engine publishes ports as iptables DNAT rules and masquerades outbound traffic.
On Kubernetes, kube-proxy programs iptables or IPVS rules that DNAT Services to pod IPs.
KVM VMs attach to a Linux bridge through tap devices.

howItWorks.title: Alternatives
howItWorks.body:
nftables: the successor to iptables; choose it for new rule sets.
Open vSwitch: choose it for VLAN-heavy or SDN-style virtual switching.
Cilium with eBPF: replaces kube-proxy rules on Kubernetes nodes.
Cloud VPC networking: managed routing and security groups instead of host configuration.

flow: A process in namespace a1 sends a packet to 10.0.2.11 on another subnet.
a1 uses its default route to 10.0.1.1 and ARPs for the gateway.
The frame crosses the veth pair into bridge br-a and is switched by MAC.
The router sees a non-local destination; ip_forward=1 sends it to the route lookup.
FORWARD permits it; the kernel emits it on br-b towards b1.
Internet-bound traffic is rewritten by POSTROUTING MASQUERADE; conntrack tracks it.
Replies are un-NATed and routed back across the bridge to a1.

deploy.summary: Build a routed network from namespaces, add VRRP, then harden SSH and serve DNS.
prerequisites: Linux VM or host with root, iproute2 and iptables
Disposable machine: the lab changes forwarding and firewall rules
Two hosts on one L2 segment for the VRRP step
Ubuntu 22.04 or 24.04 for the SSH and DNS steps

steps.title: 1. A veth pair between two namespaces
steps.code:
sudo ip netns add x
sudo ip netns add y
sudo ip link add vx type veth peer name vy
sudo ip link set vx netns x
sudo ip link set vy netns y
sudo ip -n x addr add 10.99.0.1/24 dev vx
sudo ip -n y addr add 10.99.0.2/24 dev vy
sudo ip -n x link set vx up
sudo ip -n y link set vy up
sudo ip netns exec x ping -c 2 10.99.0.2
sudo ip netns del x; sudo ip netns del y
steps.note: Deleting a namespace destroys its veth end and the peer with it. This is the virtual cable in isolation.

steps.title: 2. Bridges, two subnets and routing
steps.code:
sudo ip link add br-a type bridge
sudo ip addr add 10.0.1.1/24 dev br-a
sudo ip link set br-a up
for n in a1 a2; do
  i=$([ "$n" = a1 ] && echo 11 || echo 12)
  sudo ip netns add $n
  sudo ip link add veth-$n type veth peer name eth0 netns $n
  sudo ip link set veth-$n master br-a up
  sudo ip -n $n addr add 10.0.1.$i/24 dev eth0
  sudo ip -n $n link set eth0 up
  sudo ip -n $n link set lo up
  sudo ip -n $n route add default via 10.0.1.1
done
sudo ip netns exec a1 ping -c 2 10.0.1.12
bridge fdb show br br-a

sudo ip link add br-b type bridge
sudo ip addr add 10.0.2.1/24 dev br-b
sudo ip link set br-b up
sudo ip netns add b1
sudo ip link add veth-b1 type veth peer name eth0 netns b1
sudo ip link set veth-b1 master br-b up
sudo ip -n b1 addr add 10.0.2.11/24 dev eth0
sudo ip -n b1 link set eth0 up
sudo ip -n b1 link set lo up
sudo ip -n b1 route add default via 10.0.2.1

sudo sysctl -w net.ipv4.ip_forward=0
sudo ip netns exec a1 ping -c 1 -W 1 10.0.2.11 || echo "fails: forwarding off"
sudo sysctl -w net.ipv4.ip_forward=1
sudo ip netns exec a1 ping -c 2 10.0.2.11
steps.note: The root namespace owns 10.0.1.1 and 10.0.2.1 and is the router. If the last ping fails, check for a Docker FORWARD DROP policy.

steps.title: 3. NAT to the outside with MASQUERADE
steps.code:
UPLINK=$(ip route show default | awk '{print $5; exit}')
echo "uplink: $UPLINK"
sudo iptables -t nat -A POSTROUTING -s 10.0.1.0/24 -o "$UPLINK" -j MASQUERADE
sudo iptables -I FORWARD -i br-a -o "$UPLINK" -j ACCEPT
sudo iptables -I FORWARD -i "$UPLINK" -o br-a -m conntrack --ctstate RELATED,ESTABLISHED -j ACCEPT
sudo ip netns exec a1 ping -c 2 1.1.1.1
sudo iptables -t nat -L POSTROUTING -n -v
steps.note: The MASQUERADE packet counter must rise. These rules do not survive a reboot, which suits a lab.

steps.title: 4. Inspect like an operator
steps.code:
ip -br addr
ip route
sudo ip netns exec a1 ip route get 10.0.2.11
ip neigh show dev br-a
sudo ip netns exec b1 tcpdump -ni eth0 icmp &
sudo ip netns exec a1 ping -c 2 10.0.2.11
sudo kill %1
sudo conntrack -L 2>/dev/null | head
steps.note: ip route get shows the route and source the kernel would pick. tcpdump shows 10.0.1.11 unchanged between internal subnets: no NAT.

steps.title: 5. VRRP floating IP with keepalived (two hosts)
steps.note: The BACKUP uses state BACKUP and a lower priority. Cloud networks usually drop VRRP; use the provider's floating IP there.

steps.title: 6. Clean up the lab
steps.code:
sudo iptables -t nat -D POSTROUTING -s 10.0.1.0/24 -o "$UPLINK" -j MASQUERADE
sudo iptables -D FORWARD -i br-a -o "$UPLINK" -j ACCEPT
sudo iptables -D FORWARD -i "$UPLINK" -o br-a -m conntrack --ctstate RELATED,ESTABLISHED -j ACCEPT
for n in a1 a2 b1; do sudo ip netns del $n; done
sudo ip link del br-a; sudo ip link del br-b
sudo sysctl -w net.ipv4.ip_forward=0
steps.note: Run in the shell from step 3 so $UPLINK is set. Remove any FORWARD ACCEPT rules you added by hand.

steps.title: 7. SSH setup and hardening
steps.code:
# On your workstation: create a key and install it
ssh-keygen -t ed25519 -C "ops@site"
ssh-copy-id -i ~/.ssh/id_ed25519.pub ops@10.0.0.10
ssh ops@10.0.0.10 true        # prove key login BEFORE hardening

# On the server: drop-in config, test, then reload
sudo tee /etc/ssh/sshd_config.d/10-hardening.conf >/dev/null <<'EOF'
PermitRootLogin no
PasswordAuthentication no
KbdInteractiveAuthentication no
PubkeyAuthentication yes
AllowUsers ops
MaxAuthTries 3
LoginGraceTime 30
X11Forwarding no
EOF
sudo sshd -t && sudo systemctl reload ssh
sudo sshd -T | grep -Ei 'permitrootlogin|passwordauthentication|allowusers'

# Brute-force bans
sudo apt-get install -y fail2ban
printf '[sshd]\nenabled = true\nmaxretry = 5\nbantime = 1h\n' | sudo tee /etc/fail2ban/jail.d/sshd.local
sudo systemctl enable --now fail2ban
sudo fail2ban-client status sshd
steps.note: Keep a second session open until key login is proven. The service name is sshd on RHEL; replace ops and the IP.

steps.title: 8. DNS bring-up with dnsmasq
steps.code:
# Free port 53 (Ubuntu: disable the systemd-resolved stub listener)
sudo sed -i 's/^#\?DNSStubListener=.*/DNSStubListener=no/' /etc/systemd/resolved.conf
sudo ln -sf /run/systemd/resolve/resolv.conf /etc/resolv.conf
sudo systemctl restart systemd-resolved
sudo apt-get install -y dnsmasq dnsutils

sudo tee /etc/dnsmasq.d/lab.conf >/dev/null <<'EOF'
listen-address=127.0.0.1,10.0.0.2
bind-interfaces
domain-needed
bogus-priv
domain=lab.local
local=/lab.local/
no-resolv
server=1.1.1.1
server=9.9.9.9
cache-size=1000
host-record=node1.lab.local,10.0.0.10
address=/node2.lab.local/10.0.0.20
ptr-record=20.0.0.10.in-addr.arpa,node2.lab.local
EOF
sudo dnsmasq --test && sudo systemctl restart dnsmasq

dig @10.0.0.2 node1.lab.local +short
dig @10.0.0.2 node2.lab.local +short
dig @10.0.0.2 -x 10.0.0.10 +short
dig @10.0.0.2 -x 10.0.0.20 +short
dig @10.0.0.2 example.com | grep -E 'status|Query time'
dig @10.0.0.2 example.com | grep 'Query time'   # second run: cached
steps.note: host-record creates A and PTR; address plus ptr-record shows them separately. Replace 10.0.0.x and lab.local with your plan.

verify: Bridge: ip netns exec a1 ping -c2 10.0.1.12 works; bridge fdb show br br-a lists both MACs.
Routing: ping a1 to b1 fails with ip_forward=0 and passes with 1.
NAT: iptables -t nat -L POSTROUTING -n -v shows a rising MASQUERADE counter.
SSH: sshd -T | grep -Ei 'passwordauthentication|permitrootlogin' and ssh root@host is refused.
pitfalls: No return or default route in the namespace: packets leave, replies never arrive.
Docker or firewalld FORWARD DROP silently breaks routed lab traffic.
sysctl -w is not persistent; write /etc/sysctl.d/ files on real routers.
Overlapping CIDRs across lab, VPN and cloud produce odd routes; check ip route get.
VRRP blocked on protocol 112 makes both nodes claim the VIP.
Locking yourself out: disable password login only after key login works.
dnsmasq fails to start while systemd-resolved still holds port 53.
keyPoints: Namespaces isolate stacks; veth pairs are cables; bridges are L2 switches.
ip_forward plus MASQUERADE turns a host into a NAT router.
keepalived VRRP floats one IP between two nodes.
Key-only sshd and dnsmasq records make a bare VM reachable and named.
quickDeploy: Create a veth pair between two namespaces.
Add a bridge, a second subnet and routing.
Harden sshd, then serve DNS with dnsmasq.
osiNote: L1 NIC, L2 bridge, L3 routing and NAT, L4 conntrack and ports.
production: Persist sysctls in /etc/sysctl.d and rules in nftables.conf.
Document the IP plan; check overlaps with ip route get.
Default-deny firewall; allow SSH only from the admin subnet.
Run two keepalived nodes; test failover under ping.
Alert on link errors, conntrack table usage and VRRP state changes.
